check: what Test-S5Release.ps1 will actually do given the known version-string failure
why: It is the second post-profile step, and the release gate is known to fail on the version string. Running it expecting success would produce a false alarm; skipping it would drop the reproducibility check. Its real behaviour needed tracing in advance.
trace: verifyReleaseArtifacts collects errors and throws a GradleException when the list is non-empty, so the build fails rather than reporting a soft FAIL
The version check adds an error whenever mod_version is not exactly 0.1.0, and it is 0.1.0-s1c-preview.2
A thrown GradleException makes gradle exit non-zero, so both builds in the script will report a non-zero exitCode
The script computes passed as both exit codes zero and both SHAs matching, so passed will be false
It then writes execution.json with passed false and throws a message telling the reader to preserve the evidence
conclusion: Run as-is it will fail, and the failure is the gate correctly refusing to sign a preview. That is the expected outcome rather than a surprise to be debugged.

whatItStillDelivers.shaComparison: Both builds still run and both remapJar SHAs are captured, so remapJarShaMatch is recorded even though passed is false
whatItStillDelivers.evidence: execution.json is written before the throw, so the evidence survives and the throw message points at it
whatItStillDelivers.offlineFlags: Both builds carry the offline and strict dependency-verification flags, which is what re-exercises the offline path at current source and closes the item dated earlier this session

howToReadTheResult: Read execution.json rather than the exit status. remapJarShaMatch true with identical SHAs is the reproducibility result; passed false is the version gate, which is already recorded in the ledger under version-lock and full-package.
